transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Taking care of my mom on top of work has thrown my whole life off, and I feel like I’m not handling any of it the way I usually would. It has just been incredibly overwhelming trying to manage her care while keeping up with my job at the shop, and I feel completely out of my depth.

Beyond feeling overwhelmed by your current responsibilities, have you been experiencing persistent low mood, loss of interest in things you usually enjoy, or significant changes in your sleep or appetite over the last few weeks?

Yes, I've really been struggling with all of that. I find myself crying in the restroom at work, snapping at my coworkers, and then lying awake at night beating myself up. I've also completely stopped going to church and my truck club meets because I'm just too exhausted and overwhelmed to handle any of it.

Do you feel that your current low mood and loss of interest are primarily a reaction to the specific stress of caring for your mother, or do you feel these symptoms have taken on a life of their own regardless of the situation?

These feelings are definitely tied directly to the stress of caring for my mom right now. I really believe that if her health stabilizes or if I can get some relief from this heavy caregiving load, I'll be able to get back to my normal routine. I don't think I would feel this strung out and overwhelmed if that situation improved.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms (depressed mood, irritability, social withdrawal, sleep disturbance) developed as a direct, maladaptive response to an identifiable psychosocial stressor (caregiving responsibilities). The symptoms are clearly linked to the stressor and are expected to resolve once the stressor is removed or adapted to, fitting the criteria for adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood.
